findings.reason: The authentic original standalone tile contains the transition formula and boundary discussion but no graph. A compact graph materially clarifies the asymmetry between bidirectional interior moves and absorbing endpoint loops; a separate N=1 panel prevents suggesting interior states exist in that edge case. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a defect in the existing proof.

correction: Appended explanatory Remarks and one TikZ fence containing two transition graphs. Every original byte is preserved as a prefix, including all frontmatter, statement, Facts and Verification. No status or other protected metadata changed.

diagram_math_checks.evidence: The N=4 panel has exactly S={0,1,2,3,4}; directed edges represent entries of P:S×S→[0,1], not sample paths. The N=1 panel has exactly S={0,1}. Both are specializations of the unchanged Statement, lines 27–32.

For N=4 the six neighbor arrows are 1→0 (q), 1→2 (p), 2→1 (q), 2→3 (p), 3→2 (q), 3→4 (p). Each is precisely P(x,x−1)=q or P(x,x+1)=p for 0<x<N. There are no other interior edges or interior loops. Since q=1−p, the two outgoing weights at every interior state sum to one, as in Verification 1.1.

The top panel has one weight-1 self-loop at each of 0 and 4, and no outward arrows from those vertices. The lower panel has one weight-1 self-loop at each of 0 and 1 with no edge between them, matching the absence of interior rows when N=1 (Verification 1.1). This agrees with F1 and the absorbed-kernel definition: each x∈D has Dirac row δ_x.

The prose instructs that zero-labelled arrows are omitted. At p=0 the p-arrows vanish and q=1, leaving deterministic leftward interior transitions; at p=1 the q-arrows vanish, leaving deterministic rightward transitions. The figure asserts only one-step transitions, with no assertion of finite hitting on every path. Verification 1.2 and 2.1 retain their finite-hit event convention unchanged.

The original complete three-step Verification is byte-identical and precedes Remarks. Its row calculation, stopping-time event identity and application of F3 do not refer to the figure; the new explanatory prose explicitly preserves this independence.
